messages.author: fca2ddc6dfc88f2a
messages.subject: Moderation in Actor-Partner Interdependence Model
parts:
I have been implementing an actor-partner interdependence model in lavaan (individuals nested in couples). I would now like to add a categorical level-2 moderator, but I am unsure how to go about. Below is the syntax I have so far (it works), but I am unsure how to add the moderator.

APIM_sDpW.TD_flood.model.SPE  <- '
           flood_W ~ a1*sDpW_W
           flood_M ~ a2*sDpW_M
           flood_W ~ p12*sDpW_M
           flood_M ~ p21*sDpW_W
           sDpW_W ~ mx1*1
           sDpW_M ~ mx2*1
           flood_W ~ my1*1
           flood_M ~ my2*1
           sDpW_W ~~ vx1*sDpW_W
           sDpW_M ~~ vx2*sDpW_M
           flood_W ~~ vy1*flood_W
           flood_M ~~ vy2*flood_M
           sDpW_M ~~ cx*sDpW_W
           flood_M ~~ cy*flood_W
           flood_W ~a1b*TD_WLo
           flood_M ~a2b*TD_MLo
           flood_W ~p12b*TD_MLo
           flood_M ~p21b*TD_WLo
           TD_WLo ~mx1b*1
           TD_MLO ~mx2b*1
           TD_WLO ~~ vx1b*TD_WLO
           TD_MLO ~~ vx1b*TD_MLO
           TD_MLO ~~ cxb*TD_WLO
           sDpW_W ~~ c1*TD_WLO
           sDpW_W ~~ c2*TD_MLO
           sDpW_M ~~ c3*TD_MLO
           sDpW_M ~~ c4*TD_WLO
           ab_diff:=a1b - a2b
           pb_diff:=p12b - p21b
           k1b:=p12b/a1
           k2b:=p21b/a2
           kb_diff:=k1b - k2b
           ab_ave:=(a1b + a2b)/2
           pb_ave:=(p12b  + p 21b)/2
           sum1b:=(p12b + a1b)/2
           sum2b:=(p21b + a2b)/2
           cont1b:=a1b - p12b
           cont2b:=a2b - p21b
           a_diff:=a1 - a2
           p_diff:=p12 - p21
           k1:=p12/a1
           k2:=p21/a2
           k_diff:=k1 - k1
           i_diff:=my1 - my2
           a_ave:=(a1 + a2)/2
           p_ave:=(p12  + p 21)/2
           i_ave:=(my1  + my2)/2
           sum1:=(p12  + a1)/2
           sum2:=(p21  + a2)/2
           cont1:=a1 - p12
           cont2:=a1 - p21
            '
Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderation in Actor-Partner Interdependence Model
parts:
individuals nested in couples

But the APIM in SEM puts dyads in wide format, so there is no nesting of rows within dyads (members of dyads instead have data stored in different columns, as your variables indicate).
I would now like to add a categorical level-2 moderator, but I am unsure how to go about.

You can either include its dummy code(s) as exogenous predictor(s), which is the familiar approach from regression models:  https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Or you can use it to run a multigroup model:  https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
In the latter, moderation is implicit when a parameter (e.g., regression slope) is allowed to vary across groups.
  
Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Moderation in Actor-Partner Interdependence Model
parts: I can't figure out why the estimates are identical in both groups

Does your syntax only provide a single label?  Pass a vector of labels (1 per group), which can be different or identical, the latter of which implies equality:

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts: Am I correct that moderation does indeed occur
No one can know, but using alpha = .05, you can reject the H0 that the entire set of group-differences is zero.
but that there is no difference between the regression coefficients in the two groups (values highlighted in yellow)?

The differences are nonzero, but the degree to which they differ from the H0 of no moderation is consistent with what you can expect from sampling error alone when H0 is true.  You are estimating several parameters for such small sample sizes, so you can't expect a lot of power to detect effects that aren't veeery large.
how would I be able to compute fit indices for each group?

Does it make sense to?  If there are NO equality constraints across groups, then the results would be equivalent if you fit the model separately to each group.  If there are equality constraints across groups, then the chi-squared statistic cannot be partitioned into this or that group's misspecification, so you can't have group-specific indices based on chi-squared.  You can get group-specific standardized/correlation residuals, as well as their average (SRMR / CRMR) from lavResiduals()
